summary: A global bond rout — led by longer-dated Treasuries most vulnerable to accelerating inflation — carried over into this week as the Iran war's energy shock keeps rate-hike bets alive. The Trump-Xi Beijing summit ended without progress on reopening the Strait of Hormuz, leaving oil elevated and inflation pressure intact.
tweet: Bond yields near multi-year highs after last week's global rout, as Iran's Strait of Hormuz standoff keeps oil hot and markets brace for the first Warsh-era FOMC minutes.
